name: Alligator
intro: An alligator is a big reptile that lives in swamps and rivers. Mother alligators take good care of their babies.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: An alligator is a big reptile.
It has thick, bumpy skin like armor.
Its tail is half as long as its whole body.
It has a wide, rounded snout.
Most grown alligators are longer than a bed.

sections.title: Where does it live?
sentences: American alligators live in the southeastern United States.
Many live in Florida and Louisiana.
They live in swamps, marshes, rivers, and lakes.
They like fresh water.

sections.title: What does it eat?
sentences: Alligators eat fish, frogs, turtles, and snakes.
Young alligators eat bugs, snails, and small fish.
As they grow bigger, they eat bigger animals.
An alligator can go a long time between meals.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: A mother alligator builds a nest of leaves and soil.
She lays her eggs inside and guards them.
The babies make little noises inside their eggs.
The mother carries her babies to the water in her mouth.
The young stay near their mother for a year or two.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: Alligators are the noisiest reptiles.
They bellow loudly to talk to each other.
An alligator can use about 3,000 teeth in its life.
Alligators keep growing their whole lives.
An alligator rests with its mouth open to cool off.
